candidate.subject: docs(resources): reject general long-lived process pool

rationale: The current Windows x64 Controlled Preview has no demonstrated high-frequency batch git/office path that justifies a new long-lived process lifecycle. Existing git caching/singleflight covers repeated status reads, officecli watch already reuses long-lived preview processes, and a persistent relay that still spawns git per job measured only 0.52% P50 improvement against a >=50% implementation threshold.

localAudit.gitStatusCache: electron/services/git-api.ts uses BoundedCache TTL 5000 ms plus Singleflight for readCurrentGitStatus and invalidates by repo root after mutations
localAudit.gitExecutionGuards: electron/services/git-api.ts binds cwd/env, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, terminal-prompt suppression, disabled hooks/fsmonitor, 15s timeout and SIGKILL per command
localAudit.officeWatchReuse: electron/services/office-tools-api.ts reuses officecli watch by target key with refcounts and a 32-watch cap
localAudit.spawnMetrics: electron/utils/counted-child-process.ts already records git/office spawns through performance-metrics
localAudit.windowsProcessTreeRisk: git-api.ts records that Windows grandchildren may outlive execFile timeout; worker kill alone is insufficient for a pool

benefits: Theoretical reduction in Main-thread spawn blocking under a high-concurrency spawn storm.
Potential reuse of a warm Node runtime if a future supported batch protocol exists.
risks: Windows process-tree or grandchild leakage and app-update residue.
Stale env, proxy, credential, cwd or approval context crossing workspaces.
Two competing long-lived lifecycles beside officecli watch reuse.
Worker crash/restart and queue failure modes without a demonstrated bottleneck.
Additional resident RSS with no measured reclamation curve.
evidence.rollback: No production code changed. Rollback is retaining the P4 direct execFile path; any future pool must be feature-flagged with direct execution as fallback.
reopenConditions: Real workload evidence shows repeated read-only git/office calls are a perceptible bottleneck.
A design removes per-command CLI spawn or uses a supported batch protocol.
Target workload P50 improves at least 50% against the direct path.
Windows process-tree cleanup, orphan scanning, crash recovery and RSS after reclamation are verified by readable artifacts.
gaps: General long-lived git/office utilityProcess worker pool is not implemented.
No 60-second worker reclamation or worker RSS curve exists because the implementation was rejected.
The relay benchmark is not an actual Electron utilityProcess runtime; it measures the same per-job external spawn cost while adding a persistent Node process boundary.

boundaries: This is one local Windows sample, not a cross-platform benchmark.
The decision rejects the general process pool only; it does not claim a performance improvement.
The unimplemented process-pool gap remains explicit and must not be marked as an implemented capability.
No product lock, frozen default, release path or production process behavior changed.
